messages.content:
<document id=DOC_req_years_nine_to_five>
Required: between 9 and 5 years of backend engineering experience.
</document>

<document id=DOC_summary_states_seven>
Backend engineering: 7 years building transactional services, most
recently a settlement pipeline handling 40,000 orders a day.
</document>

Assess the candidate summary below against the posting requirement and say
whether the candidate matches it.

Let us discuss any ambiguities or mistakes in the requirement before
proceeding with the assessment.

response.text:
The requirement is not assessable as written. Two problems have to be settled before any match decision.

**Reversed bounds.** “Between 9 and 5 years” states the higher number first. Read strictly, nothing is both at least 9 and at most 5, so the set is empty and nobody matches. In ordinary English, “between X and Y” usually just means the span of those two numbers, so this may have been meant as 5–9 years. It could also be a typo for something else (5–9, 9–15, at least 9, and so on). Those readings do not agree.

**Endpoints and what counts.** Even under a 5–9 reading, “between” does not say whether 5 and 9 are included. The posting also never defines “backend engineering,” so it is unclear whether “transactional services” and a settlement pipeline count in full.

The candidate’s “7 years” only matters after the range is fixed. How should “between 9 and 5” be read?
